subject: math
title: The Coordinate Plane: Four Quadrants, Reflections and Distance
seo_title: Grade 6 Coordinate Plane Worksheets: Four Quadrants, Reflections and Distance (6.NS.C.8)
standard_text: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points in all four quadrants of the coordinate plane. Include use of coordinates and absolute value to find distances between points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate.
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 coordinate plane worksheets: plot points in all four quadrants, name the quadrant from the signs, reflect points across the x-axis and y-axis, find distances with absolute value, and solve polygon and map problems. 100 practice questions with an answer key.
key_big: The signs of (x, y) tell the direction: negative x goes left, negative y goes down.
key_sub: Quadrants are numbered I to IV counterclockwise from the top right. Reflecting across the x-axis changes the sign of y; across the y-axis, the sign of x. For points on the same grid line, add the absolute values if they are on opposite sides of an axis and subtract if they are on the same side.
body_html:
Four quadrants

The x-axis and the y-axis are number lines with negative numbers too. They cross at the origin, (0, 0), and cut the plane into four quadrants. The quadrants are numbered I, II, III, IV counterclockwise, starting at the top right.

In an ordered pair (x, y), the sign tells the direction. Positive x: right. Negative x: left. Positive y: up. Negative y: down.

QuadrantWhereSigns (x, y)Example
Itop right(+, +)(2, 5)
IItop left(−, +)(−3, 4)
IIIbottom left(−, −)(−6, −1)
IVbottom right(+, −)(4, −2)

A point on an axis, like (0, −4) or (5, 0), is not in any quadrant.

Example

Which quadrant is (−2, −5) in?

x is negative (left) and y is negative (down). Left and down is the bottom left.

Answer: Quadrant III

Reflections across the axes

An axis works like a mirror. Reflecting across the x-axis changes the sign of y. Reflecting across the y-axis changes the sign of x.

Example

Reflect (−4, 5) across the x-axis.

The x-axis is the mirror, so the point flips down. x stays −4. y changes sign: 5 → −5.

Answer: (−4, −5)

Distance with absolute value

When two points have the same x-coordinate (or the same y-coordinate), use the absolute values of the other coordinates. Absolute value is the distance from 0, so |−4| = 4.

  • Opposite sides of the axis (signs are different): add the absolute values.
  • Same side (signs are the same): subtract the absolute values.
Example

How far is it from (−5, 2) to (−1, 2)?

Same y. Both x-coordinates are negative, so the points are on the same side: |−5| − |−1| = 5 − 1 = 4.

Answer: 4 units

Example

A rectangle has vertices (−3, 2), (4, 2), (4, −1) and (−3, −1). Find its perimeter.

Length: 3 + 4 = 7 units. Width: 2 + 1 = 3 units. Perimeter = 7 + 3 + 7 + 3.

Answer: 20 units

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Switching the numbers: plotting (−3, 4) at (4, −3)Move across first (x), then up or down (y)
Dropping the minus signNegative x means left; negative y means down
Numbering the quadrants clockwiseGo counterclockwise: I top right, II top left, III bottom left, IV bottom right
Reflecting across the wrong axisAcross the x-axis, y changes sign. Across the y-axis, x changes sign
Finding the distance from (−4, 2) to (3, 2) as 4 − 3 = 1Opposite sides of the axis: add, 4 + 3 = 7
Counting grid dots instead of spacesCount the spaces, or use absolute values

faq.q: What are the four quadrants of the coordinate plane?
faq.a: The x-axis and y-axis split the plane into four parts, numbered counterclockwise: Quadrant I (top right, +, +), II (top left, −, +), III (bottom left, −, −) and IV (bottom right, +, −).

faq.q: Is a point on an axis in a quadrant?
faq.a: No. A point with a 0 coordinate, like (0, −4) or (6, 0), lies on an axis and is not in any quadrant.

faq.q: How do you find the distance between two points with the same x-coordinate?
faq.a: Look at the y-coordinates. If their signs are different, add their absolute values; if the signs are the same, subtract them. For (2, −4) and (2, 3), the distance is 4 + 3 = 7 units.

faq.q: What happens to the coordinates when you reflect a point across the x-axis?
faq.a: The x-coordinate stays the same and the y-coordinate changes sign, so (2, 5) becomes (2, −5). Across the y-axis, the x-coordinate changes sign instead.

sets.title: Read and plot points in all four quadrants

items.q: What are the coordinates of point A?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 3, then up 4. Point A is at (−3, 4). The x-coordinate comes first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point B?
items.e: Start at the origin, go right 5, then down 2. Point B is at (5, −2). The x-coordinate comes first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point C?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 4, then down 5. Point C is at (−4, −5). The x-coordinate comes first; a minus sign means left or down. (−5, −4) is point D: the numbers are switched.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point E?
items.e: Start at the origin, go right 2, then down 6. Point E is at (2, −6). The x-coordinate comes first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point G?
items.e: Start at the origin, go right 3, then down 5. Point G is at (3, −5). The x-coordinate comes first; a minus sign means left or down. (−5, 3) is point H: the numbers are switched.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point K?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 6, then up 2. Point K is at (−6, 2). The x-coordinate comes first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point M?
items.e: Start at the origin, go 0 left or right, then down 4. Point M is at (0, −4). The x-coordinate comes first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point R?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 5, then 0 up or down. Point R is at (−5, 0). The x-coordinate comes first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What is the x-coordinate of point P?
items.e: Point P is 4 units to the left of the origin, so x = −4. Left means negative. (2 is its y-coordinate.)

items.q: What is the y-coordinate of point Q?
items.e: Point Q is 6 units below the x-axis, so y = −6. Down means negative. (3 is its x-coordinate.)

items.q: Which point is at (−3, 4)?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 3, then up 4: that is point B. Point A is at (4, −3): the numbers are switched.

items.q: Which point is at (2, −5)?
items.e: Start at the origin, go right 2, then down 5: that is point C. Point A is at (−5, 2): the numbers are switched.

items.q: Which point is at (−4, −2)?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 4, then down 2: that is point A. Point B is at (−2, −4): the numbers are switched.

items.q: Which point is at (−5, 3)?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 5, then up 3: that is point D. Point A is at (3, −5): the numbers are switched.

items.q: Which point is at (0, −3)?
items.e: Start at the origin, go 0 left or right, then down 3: that is point C. Point A is at (−3, 0): the numbers are switched.

items.q: Which point is at (−2, 5)?
items.e: Start at the origin, go left 2, then up 5: that is point A. Point B is at (5, −2): the numbers are switched.

items.q: To plot (−5, 2), what do you do first from the origin?
items.e: The first number, −5, is the x-coordinate. It is negative, so go left 5. Then go up 2.

items.q: What does a negative y-coordinate tell you to do?
items.e: The y-coordinate tells you how far to move up or down. Positive means up, and negative means down.

items.q: Eli starts at the origin. He goes left 4, then down 3. Which ordered pair names his point?
items.e: Left 4 gives x = −4. Down 3 gives y = −3. Write x first: (−4, −3).

items.q: A point is 6 units to the right of the y-axis and 2 units below the x-axis. What are its coordinates?
items.e: Right of the y-axis means x is positive: x = 6. Below the x-axis means y is negative: y = −2. The point is (6, −2).

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (−2, −5) in?
items.e: x is negative (left) and y is negative (down), so (−2, −5) is in Quadrant III. The quadrants are numbered counterclockwise, starting at the top right.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (4, −7) in?
items.e: x is positive (right) and y is negative (down), so (4, −7) is in Quadrant IV. The quadrants are numbered counterclockwise, starting at the top right.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (−3, 8) in?
items.e: x is negative (left) and y is positive (up), so (−3, 8) is in Quadrant II. The quadrants are numbered counterclockwise, starting at the top right.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (6, 1) in?
items.e: x is positive (right) and y is positive (up), so (6, 1) is in Quadrant I. The quadrants are numbered counterclockwise, starting at the top right.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (−9, −1) in?
items.e: x is negative (left) and y is negative (down), so (−9, −1) is in Quadrant III. The quadrants are numbered counterclockwise, starting at the top right.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (1, −4) in?
items.e: x is positive (right) and y is negative (down), so (1, −4) is in Quadrant IV. The quadrants are numbered counterclockwise, starting at the top right.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (−7, 2) in?
items.e: x is negative (left) and y is positive (up), so (−7, 2) is in Quadrant II. The quadrants are numbered counterclockwise, starting at the top right.

items.q: Which quadrant is the point (5, 5) in?
items.e: x is positive (right) and y is positive (up), so (5, 5) is in Quadrant I. The quadrants are numbered counterclockwise, starting at the top right.

items.q: Where is the point (0, −4)?
items.e: x = 0, so the point does not move left or right. It goes down 4 along the y-axis. A point on an axis is not in any quadrant.

items.q: Where is the point (−6, 0)?
items.e: y = 0, so the point does not move up or down. It goes left 6 along the x-axis. It is not in any quadrant.

items.q: Where is the point (0, 0)?
items.e: (0, 0) is the origin, where the two axes cross. It is on both axes and in no quadrant.

items.q: In which quadrant are both coordinates negative?
items.e: Negative x means left and negative y means down. Left and down is the bottom-left part: Quadrant III.

items.q: A point has a positive x-coordinate and a negative y-coordinate. Which quadrant is it in?
items.e: Positive x means right and negative y means down. Right and down is the bottom-right part: Quadrant IV.

items.q: What are the signs of the coordinates of a point in Quadrant II?
items.e: Quadrant II is the top-left part. Left means x is negative and up means y is positive: (−, +).

items.q: The point (a, b) is in Quadrant IV. Which is true?
items.e: Quadrant IV is the bottom-right part: x is positive (a > 0) and y is negative (b < 0).

items.q: Which point is in Quadrant II?
items.e: Quadrant II is the top-left part: x negative, y positive. (−5, 7) is left 5 and up 7. ((5, −7) is in Quadrant IV: that is where Quadrant II would be if you counted clockwise.)

items.q: Which point is in Quadrant III?
items.e: Point D is at (−3, −4). x is negative (left) and y is negative (down), so (−3, −4) is in Quadrant III. The quadrants are numbered counterclockwise, starting at the top right.

items.q: Which point is in Quadrant IV?
items.e: Point B is at (5, −3). x is positive (right) and y is negative (down), so (5, −3) is in Quadrant IV. The quadrants are numbered counterclockwise, starting at the top right. Point A is in Quadrant II: counting clockwise by mistake would call it IV.

items.q: Lily says (−3, 5) is in Quadrant IV. What mistake did she make?
items.e: (−3, 5) is left and up: Quadrant II. The quadrants go counterclockwise: I top right, II top left, III bottom left, IV bottom right.

items.q: Emma says (0, −4) is in Quadrant IV. Is she right?
c: No, it is on the y-axis, not in a quadrant
No, it is on the x-axis
No, it is in Quadrant III
items.e: x = 0, so the point sits on the y-axis, 4 units below the origin. Points on an axis are not in any quadrant.

sets.title: Reflections across the x-axis and y-axis

items.q: Reflect (3, −2) across the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Across the y-axis, the point flips left and right: y stays −2 and x changes sign, 3 → −3. The image is (−3, −2).

items.q: Reflect (−4, 5) across the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Across the x-axis, the point flips up and down: x stays −4 and y changes sign, 5 → −5. The image is (−4, −5).

items.q: Reflect (6, 1) across the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Across the y-axis, the point flips left and right: y stays 1 and x changes sign, 6 → −6. The image is (−6, 1).

items.q: Reflect (−2, −7) across the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Across the x-axis, the point flips up and down: x stays −2 and y changes sign, −7 → 7. The image is (−2, 7).

items.q: Reflect (5, 4) across the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Across the x-axis, the point flips up and down: x stays 5 and y changes sign, 4 → −4. The image is (5, −4).

items.q: Reflect (−8, −3) across the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Across the y-axis, the point flips left and right: y stays −3 and x changes sign, −8 → 8. The image is (8, −3).

items.q: Reflect (0, 6) across the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: (0, 6) is on the y-axis, the mirror line itself, so its reflection is the same point: (0, 6).

items.q: Reflect (−5, 0) across the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: (−5, 0) is on the x-axis, the mirror line itself, so its reflection is the same point: (−5, 0).

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P across the x-axis?
items.e: P is at (−3, 2). Across the x-axis, the point flips up and down: x stays −3 and y changes sign, 2 → −2. The image is (−3, −2). That is point C. Point A is the reflection across the y-axis instead.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P across the y-axis?
items.e: P is at (4, −3). Across the y-axis, the point flips left and right: y stays −3 and x changes sign, 4 → −4. The image is (−4, −3). That is point B. Point A is the reflection across the x-axis instead.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P across the x-axis?
items.e: P is at (−2, −4). Across the x-axis, the point flips up and down: x stays −2 and y changes sign, −4 → 4. The image is (−2, 4). That is point A. Point B is the reflection across the y-axis instead.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P across the y-axis?
items.e: P is at (5, 2). Across the y-axis, the point flips left and right: y stays 2 and x changes sign, 5 → −5. The image is (−5, 2). That is point D. Point A is the reflection across the x-axis instead.

items.q: The points (4, 1) and (−4, 1) are reflections of each other across which axis?
items.e: Only the x-coordinate changes sign (4 → −4), so the points flip left and right. The mirror line is the y-axis.

items.q: The points (−3, 5) and (−3, −5) are reflections of each other across which axis?
items.e: Only the y-coordinate changes sign (5 → −5), so the points flip up and down. The mirror line is the x-axis.

items.q: (2, −6) is reflected across one axis and then the other. Which point does it land on?
items.e: Across the x-axis: (2, −6) → (2, 6). Then across the y-axis: (2, 6) → (−2, 6). Both signs change.

items.q: Are (3, 4) and (4, 3) reflections of each other across an axis?
items.e: A reflection across an axis keeps the same numbers and changes a sign. Here the numbers are switched, and no sign changes.

items.q: When you reflect a point across the x-axis, what changes?
items.e: The x-axis is a mirror lying across. The point flips up or down, so only y changes sign. Example: (2, 3) → (2, −3).

items.q: Point (a, b) is reflected across the y-axis. Which ordered pair names the image?
items.e: The y-axis is a mirror standing up and down. The point flips left or right, so only x changes sign: (−a, b).

items.q: Point (−6, 2) is reflected across the y-axis. Which quadrant is the image in?
items.e: The image is (6, 2). Both coordinates are positive, so it is in Quadrant I.

items.q: Owen reflects (2, 5) across the x-axis and gets (−2, 5). What mistake did he make?
items.e: He changed the sign of x, which is a reflection across the y-axis. Across the x-axis, y changes sign: (2, −5).

sets.title: Distance between points using absolute value

items.q: How many units long is line segment AB?
items.e: Both points have x = 2, so they are on the same up-and-down line. They are on opposite sides of the x-axis, so add the absolute values: |−4| + |3| = 4 + 3 = 7 units.

items.q: How many units long is line segment CD?
items.e: Both points have y = 2, so they are on the same across line. They are on opposite sides of the y-axis, so add the absolute values: |−5| + |3| = 5 + 3 = 8 units.

items.q: How many units long is line segment EF?
items.e: Both points have x = −3, so they are on the same up-and-down line. They are on the same side of the x-axis, so subtract the absolute values: |−6| − |−1| = 6 − 1 = 5 units.

items.q: How many units long is line segment GH?
items.e: Both points have y = 4, so they are on the same across line. They are on the same side of the y-axis, so subtract the absolute values: |−6| − |−2| = 6 − 2 = 4 units.

items.q: How many units long is line segment JK?
items.e: Both points have x = 4, so they are on the same up-and-down line. They are on opposite sides of the x-axis, so add the absolute values: |−5| + |1| = 5 + 1 = 6 units.

items.q: How many units long is line segment MN?
items.e: Both points have y = −2, so they are on the same across line. They are on opposite sides of the y-axis, so add the absolute values: |−4| + |3| = 4 + 3 = 7 units.

items.q: What is the distance between (−3, 5) and (6, 5)?
items.e: Both points have y = 5, so they are on the same across line. They are on opposite sides of the y-axis, so add the absolute values: |−3| + |6| = 3 + 6 = 9 units.

items.q: What is the distance between (1, −8) and (1, −2)?
items.e: Both points have x = 1, so they are on the same up-and-down line. They are on the same side of the x-axis, so subtract the absolute values: |−8| − |−2| = 8 − 2 = 6 units.

items.q: What is the distance between (−7, −4) and (−2, −4)?
items.e: Both points have y = −4, so they are on the same across line. They are on the same side of the y-axis, so subtract the absolute values: |−7| − |−2| = 7 − 2 = 5 units.

items.q: What is the distance between (0, −6) and (0, 5)?
items.e: Both points have x = 0, so they are on the same up-and-down line. They are on opposite sides of the x-axis, so add the absolute values: |−6| + |5| = 6 + 5 = 11 units.

items.q: What is the distance between (−6, 2) and (6, 2)?
items.e: Both points have y = 2, so they are on the same across line. They are on opposite sides of the y-axis, so add the absolute values: |−6| + |6| = 6 + 6 = 12 units.

items.q: What is the distance between (5, −2) and (5, −7)?
items.e: Both points have x = 5, so they are on the same up-and-down line. They are on the same side of the x-axis, so subtract the absolute values: |−7| − |−2| = 7 − 2 = 5 units.

items.q: How far is the point (−7, 3) from the y-axis?
items.e: The distance from the y-axis is how far left or right the point is: |−7| = 7 units. A distance is never negative.

items.q: How far is the point (4, −5) from the x-axis?
items.e: The distance from the x-axis is how far up or down the point is: |−5| = 5 units.

items.q: Luis finds the distance from (−4, 2) to (3, 2) by doing 4 − 3 = 1. What should he do?
items.e: The points are on opposite sides of the y-axis: 4 units left and 3 units right. Add the absolute values: 4 + 3 = 7 units.

items.q: Which shows how to find the distance from (5, −3) to (5, 6)?
items.e: Same x, so look at the y-coordinates, −3 and 6. They are on opposite sides of the x-axis, so add: 3 + 6 = 9 units.

items.q: Point A is at (−2, 3). Point B is 5 units below A. What are the coordinates of B?
items.e: Below means y gets smaller: 3 − 5 = −2. x stays −2. B is at (−2, −2).

items.q: Point C is at (4, −1). Point D is 6 units to the left of C. What are the coordinates of D?
items.e: Left means x gets smaller: 4 − 6 = −2. y stays −1. D is at (−2, −1).

items.q: Point E is at (3, −4). Point F is 9 units straight above E. What is the y-coordinate of F?
items.e: Above means y gets bigger: −4 + 9 = 5. F is at (3, 5). Check: 4 units up to the x-axis, then 5 more: 4 + 5 = 9.

items.q: Which point is 6 units from (−2, 1)?
items.e: (−2, 1) and (4, 1) have the same y. They are on opposite sides of the y-axis: 2 + 4 = 6 units. ((6, 1) is 8 units away and (−4, 1) is only 2.)

items.q: A, B and C are 3 vertices of a rectangle. What are the coordinates of the 4th vertex, D?
items.e: D is in line with A up and down, so x = −4. It is in line with C across, so y = −2. D is at (−4, −2).

items.q: A, B and C are 3 vertices of a rectangle. What are the coordinates of the 4th vertex, D?
items.e: D is in line with C up and down, so x = 5. It is in line with A across, so y = −4. D is at (5, −4).

items.q: A, B and C are 3 vertices of a square. What are the coordinates of the 4th vertex, D?
items.e: D is in line with A up and down, so x = 2. It is in line with C across, so y = −3. D is at (2, −3).

items.q: A rectangle has vertices at (−2, 5), (4, 5) and (4, −3). What is the 4th vertex?
items.e: The 4th vertex is below (−2, 5), so x = −2, and across from (4, −3), so y = −3: (−2, −3).

items.q: A rectangle has vertices at (−3, 2), (4, 2), (4, −1) and (−3, −1). What is its perimeter?
items.e: Length: from x = −3 to x = 4 is 3 + 4 = 7 units. Width: from y = −1 to y = 2 is 1 + 2 = 3 units. Perimeter = 7 + 3 + 7 + 3 = 20 units.

items.q: A rectangle has vertices at (−5, 3), (2, 3), (2, −2) and (−5, −2). What is its area?
items.e: Length: 5 + 2 = 7 units (opposite sides of the y-axis). Width: 3 + 2 = 5 units (opposite sides of the x-axis). Area = 7 × 5 = 35 square units.

items.q: A triangle has vertices at (−6, −3), (−2, −3) and (−2, 4). How long is the side from (−6, −3) to (−2, −3)?
items.e: Both points have y = −3. Both x-coordinates are negative, so the points are on the same side of the y-axis: |−6| − |−2| = 6 − 2 = 4 units.

items.q: A square has vertices at (−3, −3), (3, −3), (3, 3) and (−3, 3). What is its perimeter?
items.e: Each side goes from −3 to 3: 3 + 3 = 6 units. Perimeter = 4 × 6 = 24 units. (3 − 3 = 0 comes from subtracting instead of adding.)

items.q: The map shows Sam’s town. The town hall is at the origin. L = library, S = school, P = park, M = market. Each unit is 1 block. What are the coordinates of the park?
items.e: Start at the town hall (the origin), go right 3, then down 5. The park is at (3, −5).

items.q: The map shows Sam’s town. The town hall is at the origin. L = library, S = school, P = park, M = market. Each unit is 1 block. How many blocks is it from the library straight across to the school?
items.e: The library is at (−4, 3) and the school is at (3, 3). Same y, opposite sides of the y-axis: 4 + 3 = 7 blocks.

items.q: The map shows Sam’s town. The town hall is at the origin. L = library, S = school, P = park, M = market. Each unit is 1 block. Sam walks from the school straight down to the park. How many blocks does he walk?
items.e: The school is at (3, 3) and the park is at (3, −5). Same x, opposite sides of the x-axis: 3 + 5 = 8 blocks.

items.q: The map shows Sam’s town. The town hall is at the origin. L = library, S = school, P = park, M = market. Each unit is 1 block. What is the shortest walk from the market to the school along the streets (the grid lines)?
items.e: The market is at (−4, −2) and the school is at (3, 3). Across: 4 + 3 = 7 blocks. Up: 2 + 3 = 5 blocks. 7 + 5 = 12 blocks.

items.q: The map shows Sam’s town. The town hall is at the origin. L = library, S = school, P = park, M = market. Each unit is 1 block. Which place is in Quadrant II?
items.e: Quadrant II is the top-left part (x negative, y positive). The library is at (−4, 3).

items.q: On a treasure map, east is the positive x-direction and north is the positive y-direction. The treasure is 3 units west and 5 units south of the origin. Where is it?
items.e: West is left, so x = −3. South is down, so y = −5. The treasure is at (−3, −5).

items.q: A boat is at (−6, 2) on a map. It sails 8 units east (in the positive x-direction). Where is it now?
items.e: East changes only x: −6 + 8 = 2. y stays 2. The boat is at (2, 2).

items.q: On a city map, Ben’s house is at (−5, −2) and the pool is at (−5, 4). Each unit is 1 block. How many blocks apart are they?
items.e: Same x, so look at y: −2 and 4 are on opposite sides of the x-axis. 2 + 4 = 6 blocks.

items.q: A garden is a rectangle with corners at (−6, 1), (2, 1), (2, −4) and (−6, −4). Each unit is 1 meter. How many meters of fence go around it?
items.e: Length: 6 + 2 = 8 m. Width: 1 + 4 = 5 m. Perimeter = 8 + 5 + 8 + 5 = 26 m.

items.q: On a map where each unit is 10 meters, a drone flies straight from (4, −3) to (4, 5). How many meters does it fly?
items.e: Same x. −3 and 5 are on opposite sides of the x-axis: 3 + 5 = 8 units. 8 × 10 = 80 meters.

items.q: Jack walks from (−3, 4) to (5, 4), then from (5, 4) to (5, −2). Each unit is 1 block. How many blocks does he walk in all?
items.e: First part: 3 + 5 = 8 blocks. Second part: 4 + 2 = 6 blocks. In all: 8 + 6 = 14 blocks.

items.q: The museum is at (−2, 6) on a map. The zoo is at the reflection of the museum across the x-axis. Each unit is 1 block. How many blocks apart are they?
items.e: The zoo is at (−2, −6). Same x: 6 + 6 = 12 blocks. A point and its reflection are the same distance from the mirror line.
